Q: Trouble clicking on a button with selenium in a modal A:

Some feedback...

  1. There's really no reason to use an XPath for an ID. That's what By.ID() is for. It's simpler and more readable.

  2. If you are dealing with modals, you really need to add a WebDriverWait. There's really no reason to not use waits everywhere... it prevents failures like this and a lot of intermittent failures that can cause havoc.

  3. If you are trying to take a screenshot of the page after the modal disappears, you should add a wait using EC.invisibility_of_element_located() to make sure that the modal is gone before taking the screenshot.

Updated code...

from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By
from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC
from selenium.webdriver.support.wait import WebDriverWait

url = 'https://www.google.com'
driver = webdriver.Chrome()
driver.maximize_window()
driver.get(url)

wait = WebDriverWait(driver, 10)

button_locator = (By.ID, "continue-button") # since this is an ID, it should be unique on the page
# button_locator = (By.CSS_SELECTOR, "#content-overlay #continue-button") # if the ID isn't unique, we can be more specific by including the modal's ID in the CSS selector

wait.until(EC.element_to_be_clickable(button_locator)).click()
wait.until(EC.invisibility_of_element_located(button_locator))
# take screenshot of the page after the modal is closed

Q: How to set the http.max_content_length value for ElasticSearch container using docker container? A:

How about adding this line to Dockerfile?

RUN echo "http.max_content_length: 300M" >> /usr/share/elasticsearch/config/elasticsearch.yml

Q: Setting file path location in yaml A:

If you have something that processes the yaml check the documentation for variables. For Instance on serverless they use variables to make it dynamic, it involves using "$" but other systems use different notation:

# configuration
config:
  json_location: ${file(./config.json):PATH}

Q: how to call function/method form one class to another class in selenium webdriver using java A:

This might sound harsh, but first of all you should read about

  • Null Pointer Exception from this link.
  • How to debug from a StackTrace from this link.
  • Why using absolute xpath, or xpaths locators in general is a bad strategy from here.

From your stack trace,

Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException at Test_package_Ted_baker.search.search_1(search.java:14) at Test_package_Ted_baker.SHopping.main(SHopping.java:16)

I see that your code in Search class 

WebElement Search_Item=driver.findElement(By.xpath("html/body/div[2]/header/div/nav[2]/section/ul[2]/li[1]/a/span[1]"));

is not correct. I suspect your locator is not correct for this one. The element can easily be identified using an id attribute, as

 driver.findElement(By.id("search"));

or , if you're using xpaths, then

 driver.findElement(By.xpath("//*[@id="search"]"));

should do away the NPE - but not sure since you've used a lot of absolute xpaths - which is a horrible practise.
